note: Description taken from Sands 1965 revision (in English), including the alate and soldier, with no separate worker. The original material of this species is lost and it was at one time placed in N. latifrons; Sands fixed its identity with a neotype (Njála, Sierra Leone) and notes that the 'arboreus' of Snyder 1949 is not a valid emendation (arborum is the plural genitive of arbor). The OCR misreads decimal points as hyphens or colons (e.g. I-16 = 1.16, 0:35 = 0.35), restored here by magnitude; where an individual mean is illegible only the range is cited.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Long confused with N. latifrons; Sands takes this species as the object of Smeathman's original description and designates a neotype. It differs from N. infuscatus in having no forked groove on the frons, in the female cerci being shorter than wide at the base (in N. infuscatus the cerci are as long as wide at the base), and in the soldier nasus being thicker with fewer bristles at its tip; compared with N. lujae the postclypeus is more strongly inflated and the vertex lacks the paired long bristles.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, the region between the compound eyes and the base of the genae and the postclypeus paler, yellowish brown to brown, the postclypeus with varying dark brown shading from the midline outwards; labrum yellow to yellowish brown, antennae yellowish brown to brown; pronotum dark brown with a slightly paler T-shaped mark in the middle of the anterior half; meso- and metanota, pleura and thoracic sterna yellowish brown to brown, legs yellow to yellowish brown, the ends of the femora and the bases of the tibiae slightly darker; abdominal tergites and the sides of the sternites dark brown, the middle of the sternites yellow to yellowish brown except on the last 2—3 segments; wings translucent brown, veins dark brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule behind the eyes distinctly less than a semicircle; frontal marks variable: in males from a short white line (slightly forked anteriorly) to an indistinct mark only slightly paler than the head capsule, in females from a white fine slit to an indistinct pale patch, in both sexes flat to very weakly depressed; compound eyes distinctly prominent relative to their own diameter but not large relative to head width, eye width index 2.8—3.5 (only 1 head below 3.0), nearly circular to angular-oval; ocelli small to medium, separated from the compound eyes by 1/3 of their own minimum diameter up to slightly more than that; postclypeus moderately inflated, 2.5—3.0 times wider than long, anterior margin nearly straight to distinctly wavy, posterior margin convex and rounded, slightly wavy near the outer corners; antennae 15-segmented, II slightly longer than IV, III and V subequal and slightly shorter than IV, III slightly narrower than V. Female cerci distinctly shorter than wide at the base, the tip slightly papillate. Measurements (25 specimens, 7 localities, mm): head width (across the eyes) 1.16—1.50 (mean 1.32); maximum diameter of compound eye 0.35—0.48 (mean 0.41); ocellus 0.09—0.14 × 0.13—0.20 (mean 0.11 × 0.16); ocellus to eye 0.04—0.10 (mean 0.08); pronotum width 0.93—1.18 (mean 1.04); pronotum length 0.58—0.78 (mean 0.66); hind tibia length 1.38—1.80 (mean 1.57); fore wing length 9.40—14.70 (mean 11.40).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule orange to rusty orange, nasus rusty to chestnut-brown; pronotum and antennae concolorous with the head capsule; abdominal tergites and femora yellow, sternites, tibiae and tarsi pale yellow. Head capsule nearly circular in frontal view, slightly narrowing anteriorly, nasus conical; in lateral view almost straight, sometimes very weakly concave or wavy, nasus as long as or slightly longer than the rest of the head capsule measured from the posterior margin of the antennal socket, nasus cone angle 15—25 degrees; postgenal plate slightly and evenly convex; antennae 12—13-segmented, usually 13, II and IV usually subequal and both shorter than V, V may be shorter than or equal to III. Cephalic bristles apart from the appendages are limited to 4 at the tip of the nasus, occasionally a few fine bristles behind the nasus tip, and several on the anterior margin of the postgenal plate. Abdominal tergites with scattered minute fine bristles, the posterior margins of the last 3—4 segments with longer bristles; sternite bristles shorter, with long bristles on the posterior margin. Measurements (157 specimens, 32 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.33—1.89 (mean 1.58); head width 0.75—1.13 (mean 0.93); head capsule depth 0.50—0.75 (mean 0.62); pronotum width 0.40—0.55 (mean 0.48); pronotum length 0.18—0.25 (mean 0.20); hind tibia length 0.93—1.39 (mean 1.13).
